text:
ashley.h: bringing up customer 'lynx' LoRA on rtx-10/phi model. merged lora/v0.3 into base/model-lynx-v1 then quantized to 4-bit with q8_0. quick smoke shows BLEU down ~8 pts on conv-bench and some obvious hallucinations. tagging @mike.r for merge/quant sanity :thinking:

mike.r: can you paste the exact merge + quant commands? also which tokenizer? pattern sounds like tokenizer mismatch or merge-order weight bleed.

ashley.h: sure — ran:
```
# merge
python tools/merge_lora.py --base checkpoints/base-lynx-v1 --lora loras/lynx_cust_v03 --out merged/lynx_v1_lora03
# quantize
python tools/quantize.py --model merged/lynx_v1_lora03 --bits 4 --approach q8_0 --out quant/lynx_v1_lora03_q4
```
tokenizer: huggingface/lynx-tokenizer-v2 (same as base). evaluation used conv-bench (internal) and cust-specific faq set (10k samples).

lucas.p: did you try merging then running ptq vs the quantize script? or do a fake-quant eval (no weight folding) to isolate kernel issues. also any diffs in config like layernorm eps or use_bias toggles?

ashley.h: not yet. config looks identical per model card. dropping a couple of quick metrics we saw on the eval pack:
- conv-bench: BLEU 32 -> 24 after quant (base->q4+lora)
- faq-exact-match: 0.71 -> 0.61
- ppl (validation): 12.5 -> 18.2
- hallucination rate (sampled): ~2% -> ~7%

mike.r: that ppl jump is concerning. two quick hypotheses: tokenizer mismatch (BPE merges changed) or accidental double-quant (weights already quantized in base?). can you run a merged fp16 eval to see if LoRA itself regresses before quant? also try reorder: apply quant to base then merge LoRA into quantized base (sometimes we do quant-aware merge).

tay: also check LoRA scale/fan-in. some LoRAs assume full-precision for rescaling. try cold / no-rescale option.

eval-bot: quick-eval pack created: run id run-179560-lynx-qa. tests en-pt conv-bench (subset 1k), faq-1k, and ppl-500. dashboard: https://internal-evals.local/run/run-179560-lynx-qa (results pending) :robot_face:

ashley.h: started fp16 merged eval now: command:
```
python eval/run_eval.py --model merged/lynx_v1_lora03 --dtype fp16 --suites conv-bench,faq,ppl --out results/fp16-merged.json
```
ETA ~30m.

infra-bot: scheduled a dedicated canary on dedicated-pool-small (2xA100) for A/B tests. fallback policy set to route traffic to base-fp16 if latency or top-k token divergence > threshold.

mike.r: if fp16 looks fine then quant is culprit. try two experiments in parallel: (A) quantize base then merge LoRA into q4 (quant-then-merge), (B) quant-aware fusion (simulate quant during merge). also run token-level alignment: compute average token mismatch rate on dev set.

lucas.p: small note — sometimes tokenizer special tokens (e.g., newline vs <sep>) cause BLEU to tank. run detokenized diffs and print first 50 examples of mismatches, include token ids.

ashley.h: good call. dumping first 50 mismatches now and will attach to eval dashboard. also starting experiment A and B. launching both as separate eval runs: run-179560-A and run-179560-B.

eval-bot: run-179560-A (quant-then-merge, q4) started. run-179560-B (merge-then-quant, quant-aware) started. estimated 45m.

tay: if both fail, fallback plan is to use 8-bit quant (nf4/8bit) for customer until we can fix merge path. cost hit but preserves quality. add a canary config that pins cust-lynx to fp16 for enterprise trial. :warning:

mike.r: agree. also check for tiny float scaling differences in LoRA weight file — some producers save in float16 to shrink size, that can lead to scaling issues when naive-quantized.

ashley.h: note — customer reported a small prompt engineering change recently (added system persona token). I'll test with original prompt set too.

lucas.p: ping @ashley.h after fp16 eval, if that looks good we can roll a temp mitigator (serve fp16 for lynx, enable cached prefix and aggressive batching to offset cost).

ashley.h: fp16 merged eval finished: BLEU 32 -> 31.2 (negligible), ppl 12.6, FAQ EM 0.70. So LoRA itself is fine. quant runs still in progress. initial suspicion confirmed: quant path.

mike.r: ok that's helpful. deprioritize LoRA rework. focus on quant pipeline. next steps: 1) compare weight histograms pre/post quant for a few layers, 2) try q4 with per-channel vs per-tensor setting, 3) attempt nf4 8-bit. I'll take histograms + per-channel test, @lucas.p please run nf4 8-bit baseline.

lucas.p: on it. kicking nf4-8b run now (run-179560-C).

eval-bot: run-179560-C (nf4-8bit) started.

ashley.h: thanks everyone. I'll compile a short incident note for the customer explaining root cause (quant artifact) and our immediate mitigations (pin to fp16/nf4-8bit + canary), ETA for full fix TBD after we diagnose histogram results.

mike.r: thanks. add a short test to CI that runs quant-merge smoke on a tiny sample whenever we onboard a new LoRA to catch regressions early. low cost. :thumbsup:

ashley.h: added ticket ML-2472 for CI smoke and ML-2473 for quant-investigation. assigning to @mike.r and @lucas.p. will update thread when quant runs finish.

eval-bot: run-179560-A results: BLEU 23.8, ppl 17.9, FAQ EM 0.60. run-179560-B results: BLEU 24.1, ppl 17.5, FAQ EM 0.61. run-179560-C (nf4-8bit) partial: BLEU 30.5, ppl 13.2, FAQ EM 0.69 (still running).

ashley.h: nf4 looks promising so far. I'll propose serving nf4-8bit for the customer short-term.

mike.r: solid. once nf4 is validated across larger sample we can promote and update docs on recommended quant path for LoRA merges. thanks team. :shipit:

lucas.p: logging lessons in onboarding playbook: 1) always run fp16 merged baseline, 2) prefer nf4/8bit for merged LoRAs, 3) add token-level mismatch quickchecks.

ashley.h: closing loop — will post a short summary to #customer-success after we finalize mitigation plan.
